answer: PoA resists sybils by charging an entry toll that only honest work refunds: each identity must first attest real peer txs, and the cipher guarding an answer is keyed to a one-time nonce, so a fresh clone opens with zero history and no reputation anchor. A rotating inlet of established graders samples submissions, leaving unvouched accounts unpicked while proven peers earn seats. Spinning up N fakes therefore costs N unconverged histories plus N graded answers, and none pay until a peer panel attests them, so mass identity creation burns more than one honest worker earns.
